core_invariant: The benchmark effect may run only the fixed reviewed synthetic workload after separate signed admission and durable one-time consumption; it cannot accept arbitrary benchmark code or inputs, inspect host telemetry, execute repository code, use a network, or create general executor authority.
trusted_inputs_required: separate valid short-lived Ed25519 laboratory admission
exact signed issued lifecycle transcript and head receipt
reviewed Linux isolation receipt for the exact revision and image
threats: reinterpreting the inert dry-run plan as effect authority without the separate admission
admission signer, revision, plan, lifecycle, compiler, isolation policy or operation substitution
unknown, stale, revoked or already-consumed lifecycle state being treated as active
starting the benchmark process before durable one-time consumption and signed consumed-head evidence
replacing the fixed benchmark script, workload, iteration count, checksum or timer source
adding arbitrary benchmark code, caller input, command, argv, shell, environment-controlled executable selection or repository bind mounts
reading host CPU, memory, process, filesystem, kernel or hardware telemetry
turning one elapsed observation into a portable machine score, hardware ranking, production SLO or capacity guarantee
network, credential, secret, package, service, remote-endpoint or contributed-hardware widening
post-consumption uncertainty being rewritten as completion rather than terminal interruption
executor receipt signer, consumed-head, final-head, isolation-image or metric-output substitution
elevating a successful bounded receipt into task success, general executor availability, deployment, capability promotion or AXIOM authority
controls: strict exact-field admission and receipt validation
fixed compiler builtin mapping with null executable and empty argv
known-active revocation input plus exact signed lifecycle verification
separately signed durable consumed-head receipt before effect
fixed iteration count and deterministic expected checksum
only monotonic elapsed nanoseconds are observed; no throughput score is derived
network none and no repository/host bind mounts
128 MiB memory, 32 PID, 0.5 CPU, non-root, read-only-root hosted Linux containment
bounded stdout and timeout with verified container cleanup
signed executor receipt and independently verified durable final head
secret-free protected workflow and release semantic guard
promotion_blockers: trusted production admission and current revocation service
operation-specific review before any non-synthetic benchmark workload
separate policy before host telemetry or repository-code measurement
explicit statistical methodology before any cross-machine comparison claim
production persistence/currentness and independent security review
